summary: The ingestion‑server experienced a transient drop in ingestion rate on 2026‑03‑03, coinciding with a burst of Kafka connection warnings and isolated Netty stream errors. The drop was brief (≈15 minutes) and was followed by a large backlog flush, indicating a temporary downstream outage rather than a node failure.

impact.description: Ingress event rate fell from ~150 k events/s to ~1 event/s, then spiked to ~250 k events/s as back‑log cleared.

trigger: Repeated failures to connect to Kafka brokers (stream‑kafka‑cluster‑kafka‑5 and -12) around 22:24 PST, suggesting a short‑lived network or broker availability issue.
rootCause: Transient network partition or Kafka broker outage at ~22:24 PST prevented the ingestion‑server from publishing events, causing the observed ingestion‑rate dip.
contributingFactors: Isolated Netty Stream Error warnings at 01:27, 12:25 and 17:30 PST (likely unrelated background noise).
Possible back‑pressure from downstream ClickHouse during the spike period.

timeline.event: WARN — Kafka NetworkClient : Error connecting to node stream‑kafka‑cluster‑kafka‑5 (producer‑1)
WARN — Kafka NetworkClient : Error connecting to node stream‑kafka‑cluster‑kafka‑12 (producer‑2)
Ingestion rate spike to ~250 k events/s as backlog flushes.

metrics: "sum(rate(ingestion_source_log_event_accepted{chart=\"ingestion-server\"}[5m]))": 150 000 events/s baseline; drop to ~1 event/s 15:30‑15:45 PST then spike to ~250 000 events/s
logs: 42 Kafka connection WARN messages around 22:24 PST (sample shown in timeline).
infra: ingestion_source_log_batch_accepted: abnormal spike 12:40 PST – 4:45 PM PST

recommendedActions: Check health and logs of Kafka brokers stream‑kafka‑cluster‑kafka‑5 and -12 for the 22:20‑22:30 PST window.
Verify network connectivity (peering, firewall, service‑mesh policies) between ingestion‑server pods and Kafka brokers.
Review ClickHouse sink metrics during the spike to see if back‑pressure contributed.
Consider adding exponential back‑off and circuit‑breaker logic to the ingestion‑server Kafka producer.
Monitor ingestion‑server queue lengths and buffer occupancy to catch future back‑pressure early.
